extracted.intended_audience: prospective Fulbright applicants and the general public (students, scholars, teachers, artists, and professionals)
extracted.subtask_description: A high-level informational overview of the Fulbright Program: its mission, scope, who it serves, and the kinds of exchange activities and awards it provides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit-based scholarships
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fulbright Program awards approximately 9,000 merit-based scholarships in the United States and more than 160 countries every year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards are intended for accomplished students, scholars, teachers, artists, and professionals of all backgrounds and fields; applicants are encouraged to 'Find a program that is right for you.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Target participants / eligibility audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Fulbright grants are for 'accomplished students, scholars, teachers, artists, and professionals of all backgrounds and fields.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program activities include studying, teaching, conducting research, exchanging ideas, and contributing to solutions for complex global challenges; the site highlights alumni across disciplines as examples of participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program mission and expected contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Fulbright's founding goal is 'to increase mutual understanding and support friendly and peaceful relations between the people of the United States and the people of other countries.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fulbrighters are expected to showcase American excellence, innovation, and culture abroad and to engage in activities that strengthen international connections and address global challenges; the program is led by the U.S. Government in partnership with over 160 countries.
